verifiedClaims.claim: the 65-mph motorway that carries Georgia Ports Authority freight out of the Garden City Terminal toward I-95 and downtown Savannah
verifiedClaims.currentValue: 65 mph is the posted limit on I-16 (SR 404) from 0.21 mi west of SR 307/Dean Forest Road (MP 160.14) to 0.20 mi west of SR 21/I-516 (MP 163.22); it drops to 55 mph from there to SR 204 (MP 165.75), 45 mph to Gwinnett Street, and 35 mph for the last 0.24 mi to the Montgomery Street terminus. GPA's designated port truck routes are the Jimmy DeLoach Parkway (a $129M limited-access truck route linking Garden City Terminal with I-16 and I-95; the 2016 connector carries 5,000 trucks a day to I-95) and the Brampton Road Connector (a $126M four-lane highway linking Gate 3 to the interstate system, opened July 2026). Port trucks reach I-16 via SR 307/Dean Forest Road (exit 160) or I-516 (exit 164), not from a terminal gate on I-16 itself.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: City of Savannah Code Sec. 207, speed limits for on-system highways (S.R. 404/I-16 rows); Georgia Ports Authority — Road; GPA press release 2026-07-07 (Brampton Road Connector)

'Carries GPA freight ... toward I-95' overstates I-16's role: GPA routes I-95-bound trucks over the Jimmy DeLoach Parkway (I-95 exit 106). verifiedClaims.claim: The Port of Savannah Garden City Terminal is the busiest single container terminal in North America. According to the Georgia Ports Authority, the terminal handled approximately 5.3 million TEUs in fiscal year 2024 — every container leaves by truck or rail, and most by truck onto I-16.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: GPA describes Garden City Terminal as 'the single largest and fastest growing container terminal in North America' (1,345 acres) — 'largest', not 'busiest'. Latest fiscal year: the Port of Savannah moved 5.67 million TEUs in FY2026 (July 1, 2025–June 30, 2026), 'just shy of the 5.7 million reached in the previous year' (FY2025, which was up 8.6% on FY2024). Calendar 2025: nearly 5.7 million TEUs, the second-busiest year on record behind 2022 (~5.9 million). GPA: '80 percent of Savannah's cargo moves inland by truck and 20 percent by rail'; the port handles 14,000–16,000 truck moves a day, Monday through Friday; 545,214 containers moved by rail in 2025.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Ports Authority — Garden City Terminal facility page; GPA press release 2026-07-28 ('Port of Savannah volumes up 18% in June', FY2026 total); GPA press release 2026-01-27 ('Port of Savannah achieves second busiest year ever'); GPA press release 2026-04-30 (trade conference; 80/20 truck-rail split)
verifiedClaims.note: Three fixes: (1) 'busiest' → GPA's own 'largest'; (2) the FY2024 figure is two fiscal years stale — use FY2026's 5.67 million TEUs; (3) 'most by truck onto I-16' is unsupported — GPA says 80% leaves by truck but routes it over the Jimmy DeLoach Parkway and Brampton Road Connector to I-95/I-516/I-16; say 'most by truck' without naming I-16 as the route. verifiedClaims.claim: Electronic logging device (ELD) data under 49 C.F.R. Part 395, post-crash drug-and-alcohol records, dashcam footage, and dispatcher communications can be lawfully overwritten in 7 to 14 days unless a preservation (spoliation) letter is sent.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: No federal rule sets a 7–14-day window. Retention floors: records of duty status (ELD data) and supporting documents — 6 months (49 CFR 395.8(k)); driver vehicle inspection reports — 3 months (49 CFR 396.11); maintenance/inspection records — 1 year and 6 months after the vehicle leaves the carrier (49 CFR 396.3(c)); drug-and-alcohol testing records — 1 to 5 years, with positive results and refusals kept 5 years (49 CFR 382.401). Dashcam video, dispatcher messages and ECM/EDR data have no federal retention rule and may be overwritten at any time.
verifiedClaims.note: '7 to 14 days' is invented and, for drug-and-alcohol records, backwards — § 382.401 requires positives and refusals to be kept five years. Keep the preservation-letter advice (litigation practice); tie the urgency to dashcam/dispatcher data, which genuinely has no floor. Published twice (Key Takeaways and FAQ 4).

verifiedClaims.claim: Chatham County is the venue. A non-felony port-truck tort case is typically filed in Chatham County State Court; felony-related or higher-damages cases go to Chatham County Superior Court (Eastern Judicial Circuit) at 133 Montgomery Street, Savannah.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: State Court of Chatham County hears civil actions 'without regard to the amount in controversy', concurrently with the Superior Court (O.C.G.A. § 15-7-4(a)); the Superior Court of Chatham County is the court of general jurisdiction and the whole of the Eastern Judicial Circuit, which 'is comprised solely of Chatham County' and expressly includes Garden City. There is no felony or damages threshold between the two for a civil suit. Both sit in the Chatham County Courthouse complex: the Tom Coleman Courthouse at 133 Montgomery Street (State Court Clerk; Superior Court judges, Suite 304) and the Judge Eugene H. Gadsden Courthouse at 400 W. Oglethorpe Avenue (Clerk of Superior Court filings, Suite 178).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Chatham County Courts — Superior Court Judges (Eastern Judicial Circuit); Chatham County Courts — Map & Directions; Chatham County Department Contacts; Georgia Code § 15-7-4 (Justia, verified run-4709)
verifiedClaims.note: 'Non-felony' and 'felony-related' are criminal categories that do not apply to civil damages suits (same finding as run-4709 for Glynn). 133 Montgomery Street is correct for both courts' courtrooms. verifiedClaims.claim: Personal auto policy, GA UM/UIM under O.C.G.A. § 33-7-11 (Georgia generally does not permit stacking)
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Georgia permits stacking of UM/UIM coverage across multiple policies (State Farm v. Hancock, 164 Ga. App. 32 (1982); Dairyland Ins. Co. v. State Farm, Ga. Ct. App. 2008); what is barred is pyramiding limits within a single policy. What decides the value of the claim is the written election under § 33-7-11(b)(1)(D)(ii) between 'added-on' coverage (the default) and 'reduced-by' coverage, plus the limits chosen under § 33-7-11(a)(1) (at least $25,000/$50,000/$25,000, or equal to liability limits unless the insured chose less).

verifiedClaims.claim: handles wrongful-death claims under O.C.G.A. § 51-4-1 et seq.

verifiedClaims.claim: Venue almost always lands in Chatham County. A non-felony tort case is filed in Chatham County State Court at 133 Montgomery Street. Felony-related or large-damages cases go to Chatham County Superior Court in the Eastern Judicial Circuit, also at 133 Montgomery Street.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: State Court of Chatham County and the Superior Court of Chatham County (Eastern Judicial Circuit, Chatham County only) have concurrent jurisdiction over civil damages suits of any amount (O.C.G.A. § 15-7-4(a)); the Superior Court also has exclusive jurisdiction over felonies, divorce, equity and title to land. Both sit at the Chatham County Courthouse complex, 133 Montgomery Street (Tom Coleman Courthouse) and 400 W. Oglethorpe Avenue (Gadsden Courthouse, where the Clerk of Superior Court accepts filings).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 15-7-4 (Justia); Chatham County Courts — Superior Court Judges; Map & Directions; Superior Court Self-Help (filing at 400 W. Oglethorpe Ave, Suite 178)
verifiedClaims.note: Rewrite: 'Most Chatham County truck-crash suits are filed in the State Court of Chatham County, which hears civil cases of any amount; the Superior Court of Chatham County (the Eastern Judicial Circuit, which is Chatham County alone and includes Garden City) can hear the same suits. Both sit at the courthouse complex at 133 Montgomery Street.' Drop 'non-felony' and 'felony-related'.

verifiedClaims.claim: The 2-year limit under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33 is hard. If the City of Garden City is a defendant (because, for example, a municipal vehicle is involved), the 6-month ante-litem notice under O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5 is harder still. A State-of-Georgia claim under O.C.G.A. § 50-21-26 has a 12-month notice window.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code §§ 9-3-33, 36-33-5, 50-21-26 (Justia); run-4709 facts pack
verifiedClaims.note: All three periods verified. Recommend adding the county rule: 'If a Chatham County vehicle is involved, the claim must be presented to the county within 12 months under O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1.' Cosmetic: the second § 50-21-26 citation in the source HTML carries a trailing period inside the citation ('§ 50-21-26.') — harmless as sentence punctuation, but make sure any statute link wraps the citation without the period.

verifiedClaims.claim: O.C.G.A. § 33-7-11 governs UM/UIM in Georgia, and unlike South Carolina, Georgia generally does not allow you to stack UM coverage across multiple policies — the offer-of-reduction form on each policy decides what coverage is "add-on" vs. "reduced by" the at-fault liability limit.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Georgia lets an insured stack UM/UIM coverage from more than one policy (Hancock 1982; Dairyland 2008); the decisive document is the written election under § 33-7-11(b)(1)(D)(ii) between 'added-on' coverage (the default, paid on top of the trucker's liability limits) and 'reduced-by' coverage (paid only above those limits). 'Offer-of-reduction form' is not a Georgia term.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 33-7-11(b)(1)(D)(ii) and annotations (Justia); Dairyland Ins. Co. v. State Farm (Ga. Ct. App. 2008); run-4709 facts pack
verifiedClaims.note: Three fixes in one sentence: the stacking rule is reversed; 'unlike South Carolina' is cross-jurisdiction law on a Georgia-only post (delete); 'offer-of-reduction form' should be the added-on/reduced-by election. The added-on vs reduced-by point itself is correct and worth keeping.

verifiedClaims.claim: For a fatal port-truck crash where the motor carrier is at the $750,000 federal minimum and damages are far higher, the UM/UIM analysis on the family's own policies can be decisive.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: 49 CFR § 387.9 (Cornell LII)
verifiedClaims.note: $750,000 minimum verified; the rest is legal reasoning.

verifiedClaims.claim: Hit by a port-freight tractor-trailer on I-16 through Garden City? A Savannah truck accident lawyer's guide to Chatham County liability, FMCSR evidence, and Georgia's 2-year deadline.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 9-3-33 (Justia)
verifiedClaims.note: Two-year deadline verified; no other factual claim. The excerpt publishes as the Article schema description.

verifiedClaims.claim: In Georgia, you have 2 years from the date of the I-16 crash to file a personal-injury lawsuit under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33. That clock does not pause while the motor carrier's insurer "investigates," and it is shorter than South Carolina's 3-year window. If a Garden City municipal employee is a defendant, an ante-litem notice is due within 6 months under O.C.G.A. § 36-33-5 — independent of the 2-year suit deadline.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: Two-year § 9-3-33 period and six-month § 36-33-5 municipal ante-litem verified. The South Carolina comparison is cross-jurisdiction law on a Georgia-only post.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code §§ 9-3-33, 36-33-5, 36-11-1 (Justia); profiles/writer-profile.md jurisdiction rules
verifiedClaims.note: Delete 'and it is shorter than South Carolina's 3-year window'. Optionally append 'and 12 months if a Chatham County vehicle is involved (O.C.G.A. § 36-11-1)'. FAQ answers publish as FAQPage structured data, so the SC reference is currently published twice.

verifiedClaims.claim: Under Georgia's modified comparative-negligence rule at O.C.G.A. § 51-12-33, you can still recover damages as long as you were less than 50% at fault for the I-16 crash. Your recovery is reduced by your percentage of fault. If you are found 50% or more responsible, you are barred from recovery.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 51-12-33(a), (g) (Justia)
verifiedClaims.note: Rule stated exactly.

verifiedClaims.claim: A fatal Garden City truck crash typically opens claims against the driver, the motor carrier (the company whose USDOT number is on the truck), the broker that arranged the load, the shipper, and sometimes the chassis pool operator and trailer owner. Federal motor-carrier insurance under FMCSA rules carries a $750,000 minimum, often $1M or more. A wrongful-death action is brought under O.C.G.A. § 51-4-1 et seq.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: 49 CFR § 387.9; 49 CFR § 390.21 (USDOT number marking) (Cornell LII); Georgia Code § 51-4-1 (Justia)
verifiedClaims.note: $750,000 minimum verified; 'often $1M or more' is hedged market observation. Optional: name the § 51-4-2 claimants (spouse, then children; parents under § 19-7-1 when neither survives).

verifiedClaims.claim: Electronic logging device (ELD) data under 49 C.F.R. Part 395, dashcam and rear-view footage, dispatcher Slack/text logs, satellite/Qualcomm pings, post-trip inspection reports under Part 396, and driver drug-and-alcohol records can all be lawfully overwritten within 7 to 14 days unless a written preservation letter is sent. The motor carrier's rapid-response adjuster is on the scene within hours — your evidence has to be locked down on the same timeline.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: ELD records of duty status: 6 months (49 CFR 395.8(k)); post-trip inspection reports (DVIRs): 3 months (49 CFR 396.11); drug-and-alcohol testing records: 1–5 years, positives and refusals 5 years (49 CFR 382.401); dashcam footage, dispatcher messages and telematics pings: no federal retention rule.
verifiedClaims.note: Rewrite the first sentence: 'Dashcam footage, dispatcher messages and telematics pings have no federal retention rule and can be overwritten at any time; federal rules let a carrier destroy post-trip inspection reports after three months (49 C.F.R. § 396.11) and ELD hours-of-service records after six (§ 395.8(k)); drug-and-alcohol test results are kept one to five years (§ 382.401).' Keep the preservation-letter and rapid-response sentences. Publishes as FAQPage schema.

verifiedClaims.claim: A 2-year statute of limitations gives you time to value the case properly under O.C.G.A. § 9-3-33; the first offer rarely reflects that value.
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 9-3-33 (Justia)
verifiedClaims.note: Only the two-year period is a factual claim; the rest is the firm's settlement-practice view.

verifiedClaims.claim: Most port-truck tort cases out of Garden City are filed in Chatham County State Court at 133 Montgomery Street, Savannah — the Court that handles non-felony tort matters in the Eastern Judicial Circuit. Felony-related or higher-damages cases go to Chatham County Superior Court. If the motor carrier is out-of-state and the amount in controversy exceeds $75,000, the case may sit in or be removed to the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Georgia, Savannah Division.
verifiedClaims.currentValue: State Court of Chatham County hears civil suits of any amount concurrently with the Superior Court (O.C.G.A. § 15-7-4(a)); 'Eastern Judicial Circuit' is the Superior Court's circuit (Chatham County alone), not a State Court label; there is no felony or damages split for civil cases. Federal: diversity plus more than $75,000 in controversy (28 U.S.C. § 1332(a)); Savannah Division covers Chatham (28 U.S.C. § 90(c)).
verifiedClaims.sourceName: Georgia Code § 15-7-4 (Justia); Chatham County Courts — Superior Court Judges; 28 U.S.C. §§ 90, 1332 (Cornell LII)
verifiedClaims.note: Replace the first two sentences with: 'Most port-truck suits out of Garden City are filed in the State Court of Chatham County at 133 Montgomery Street, Savannah, which hears civil cases of any amount; the Superior Court of Chatham County (Eastern Judicial Circuit) can hear the same cases.' The federal sentence is correct. Publishes as FAQPage schema.
